To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inhibitory effects of anti‐CD 4 on T helper functions are mediated by CD4,45RA+ and CD4,45RO+ T cell subsets.
anti‐CD4 specifically inhibits helper function of CD45RA‐ T cells, and that this effect is probably due to a contact‐inhibition in early phases of T‐B cell interactions.

the anti‐CD 4 MoAb inhibits helper functions of CD4+ T cells by affecting CD4+45RO+ T cell subset and that the inhibitory effects on T helper functions of CD 4+ 45RO+T cells are mediated by contact inhibition of T‐B interaction in early phase of collaboration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of anti‐ CD4 on helper functions in CD4,45RA+ and CD4, 4SRO+ T cells.
the effect of anti‐ CD4 on helper function in CD4,45RA+ versus 45RO+T cells.
the effects of anti‐CD 4 on the function of CD4+ T cells, with special regard to helper functions of CD4,45RO+ versus CD4,45RA+ T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anti‐CD4 is a very potent inhibitor of T cell‐mediated B cell differentiation and that this effect is due lo contact inhibition between CD4, 4SO+ T cells and B cells.

CD4,45RA+ cells are not able to function as T helper cells, whereas CD4,45RO+ cells are able to do this, and that the helper function is inhibited by anti‐ CD4 by contact inhibition of CD4,45 RO+ cells.
the anti‐CD45RA MoAbs are not suitable for depletion of CD4+ cells in clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anti‐CD4 is an effective inhibitor of T‐cell‐dependent humoral immune responses, which is due to its inhibitory effects on T‐cell functions, especially on the CD4, 4SO+ T cells.
the helper function of CD45 isoforms is not only determined by their expression on T cells, but is also regulated by the expression of CD45 on T cells.
anti‐CD4 is a useful tool for investigating the role of CD4, CD45RO and CD45RA molecules in T helper cell function in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
anti‐CD4 has a differential effect on CD4, 44RO+ versus CD4, 45RA+ T cells.
anti‐CD4 has a profound effect on the function of CD4+ cells, but that the effects are not uniform and depend upon the phenotype of the T cells.
anti‐CD4 has a differential effect on helper function of different CD4 subsets.
